newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil knocked lower despite firmer crude.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil knocked lower despite firmer crude.

text.p: Fuel oil was under pressure on Friday despite crude gaining upwards momentum.
Good supplies of Russian straight run continues to weigh on the cracked market which in certain areas was also being subjected to strong selling pressure.

High sulphur cracked fuel barges traded up to $3 lower with deals seen between $112-$114 fob ARA. Dealers said there was a concerted move to push prices lower for pricing purposes on several cargoes of Russian straight run expected in ARA next week. In addition physical shipper demand was still flabby and some sellers were keen to shift material before the end of the month.

High sulphur cargoes in NWE were peggged steady around $110-$112 fob NWE amid lacklustre interest. In the Med prices were knocked lower by aggresive sellers. One was offering material at $108 fob Med and paper has been done at $108.75.
Russian material was set to remain well offered next week giving no respite for fuel prices.
Low sulphur cracked cargoes were assessed between high fob NWE flat and high fob NWE +$1. "No buyer is interested in fixed prices, there's still room to go down," commented one trader.
